claim: Resistance to targeted cancer therapies is an important clinical problem.
source: Resistance to targeted cancer therapies is an important clinical problem.
evidence: This is a general statement about the clinical significance of drug resistance, representing established knowledge in oncology.

claim: The discovery of anti-resistance drug combinations is challenging as resistance can arise by diverse escape mechanisms.
source: The discovery of anti-resistance drug combinations is challenging as resistance can arise by diverse escape mechanisms.
evidence: This statement reflects established understanding in the field about the complexity of resistance mechanisms.

claim: The experimental-computational perturbation biology method was improved and applied in this study.
source: To address this challenge, we improved and applied the experimental-computational perturbation biology method.
evidence: The authors directly state they improved and applied their method.

claim: Network models are built from high-throughput measurements of molecular and phenotypic responses to combinatorial targeted perturbations using statistical inference.
source: Using statistical inference, we build network models from high-throughput measurements of molecular and phenotypic responses to combinatorial targeted perturbations.
evidence: This describes the methodological approach used in the study.

claim: The models are computationally executed to predict the effects of thousands of untested perturbations.
source: The models are computationally executed to predict the effects of thousands of untested perturbations.
evidence: This describes the computational capability of the models developed in the study.

claim: 143 proteomic/phenotypic entities were measured under 89 perturbation conditions in RAF-inhibitor resistant melanoma cells.
source: In RAF-inhibitor resistant melanoma cells, we measured 143 proteomic/phenotypic entities under 89 perturbation conditions
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental measurements performed.

claim: c-Myc was predicted as an effective therapeutic co-target with BRAF or MEK.
source: In RAF-inhibitor resistant melanoma cells, we measured 143 proteomic/phenotypic entities under 89 perturbation conditions and predicted c-Myc as an effective therapeutic co-target with BRAF or MEK.
evidence: This is a key prediction from the computational models.

claim: JQ1 affects the level of c-Myc protein.
source: Experiments using the BET bromodomain inhibitor JQ1 affecting the level of c-Myc protein and protein kinase inhibitors targeting the ERK pathway confirmed the prediction.
evidence: This is an experimental observation confirming the effect of JQ1 on c-Myc.

claim: Protein kinase inhibitors targeting the ERK pathway confirmed the prediction of c-Myc as a co-target.
source: Experiments using the BET bromodomain inhibitor JQ1 affecting the level of c-Myc protein and protein kinase inhibitors targeting the ERK pathway confirmed the prediction.
evidence: This describes experimental validation of the computational predictions.

claim: Co-targeting a specific upstream alteration and a general downstream point of vulnerability is proposed as an anti-cancer strategy to prevent or overcome resistance to targeted drugs.
source: In conclusion, we propose an anti-cancer strategy of co-targeting a specific upstream alteration and a general downstream point of vulnerability to prevent or overcome resistance to targeted drugs.
evidence: This is the main therapeutic hypothesis proposed based on the study findings.

claim: The inhibition of key oncogenes with target-specific agents elicits dramatic initial response in some cancers such as prostate cancer and melanoma.
source: The inhibition of key oncogenes with target-specific agents elicits dramatic initial response in some cancers such as prostate cancer and melanoma (Bollag et al., 2010; Clegg et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Drug resistance eventually emerges leading to rapid progression of metastatic disease even for the most successful single-agent targeted therapies.
source: Even for the most successful single-agent targeted therapies, however, drug resistance eventually emerges leading to rapid progression of metastatic disease (Garraway and Janne, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: The mechanism of drug resistance may involve selection of resistant sub-clones, emergence of additional genomic alterations, and compensating interactions between alternative signaling pathways.
source: The mechanism of drug resistance may involve selection of resistant sub-clones, emergence of additional genomic alterations, and compensating interactions between alternative signaling pathways (Choi et al., 2007; Huang et al., 2011; Wagle et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Combining targeted drugs to block potential escape routes is one potential solution to overcome drug resistance.
source: One potential solution to overcome drug resistance is to combine targeted drugs to block potential escape routes (Fitzgerald et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: There is currently a need for systematic strategies to develop effective drug combinations.
source: Therefore, there is currently a need for systematic strategies to develop effective drug combinations.
evidence: This is an inference based on the challenges described in drug resistance.

claim: BRAFV600E gain-of-function mutation is observed in approximately 50% of melanomas.
source: BRAFV600E gain-of-function mutation is observed in ∼50% of melanomas (Davies et al., 2002).
evidence: This is a well-established fact supported by citation.

claim: Direct inhibition of BRAFV600E by vemurafenib and inhibition of downstream MEK and ERK kinases have yielded response rates of more than 50% in melanoma patients with BRAFV600E mutation.
source: Direct inhibition of BRAFV600E by the RAF inhibitor (RAFi) vemurafenib and inhibition of the downstream MEK and ERK kinases have yielded response rates of more than 50% in melanoma patients with this mutation (Chapman et al., 2011; Flaherty et al., 2012b).
evidence: This is supported by citations to clinical trial data.

claim: Inhibition of the ERK pathway leads to changes in expression of a set of critical cell cycle genes (e.g., CCND1, MYC, FOS) and feedback inhibitors of ERK signaling (e.g., DUSP, SPRY2).
source: At the cellular level, inhibition of the ERK pathway leads to changes in expression of a set of critical cell cycle genes (e.g., CCND1, MYC, FOS) and feedback inhibitors of ERK signaling (e.g., DUSP, SPRY2) (Pratilas et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published research.

claim: Resistance to vemurafenib emerges after a period of approximately 7 months in tumors that initially responded to single-agent therapy.
source: Resistance to vemurafenib emerges after a period of ∼7 months in tumors that initially responded to single-agent therapy (Chapman et al., 2011; Sosman et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to clinical data.

claim: Multiple RAFi and MEKi resistance mechanisms have been discovered in melanoma, which may involve alterations in NRAS/ERK pathway or parallel pathways.
source: Multiple RAFi and MEKi (e.g., PD-0325901, Trametinib) resistance mechanisms, which may involve alterations in NRAS/ERK pathway (e.g., NRAS mutations, switching between RAF isoforms) or parallel pathways (e.g., PTEN loss), have been discovered in melanoma (Johannessen et al., 2010; Nazarian et al., 2010; Poulikakos et al., 2010; Xing et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to published research.

claim: The alterations associated with drug resistance may pre-exist alone, in combinations, or emerge sequentially and vary substantially between patients.
source: The alterations associated with drug resistance may pre-exist alone, in combinations, or emerge sequentially and vary substantially between patients (Van Allen et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published research.

claim: Conventional methods and combinatorial drug screens generally fail to come up with effective combinations due to the genomic complexity and heterogeneity of tumors.
source: Despite anecdotal success, conventional methods and combinatorial drug screens generally fail to come up with effective combinations due to the genomic complexity and heterogeneity of tumors (Zhao et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: System-wide models that cover interactions between tens to hundreds of signaling entities can describe and predict cellular response to multiple interventions.
source: In order to more effectively nominate drug combinations, we propose to employ system-wide models that cover interactions between tens to hundreds of signaling entities and can describe and predict cellular response to multiple interventions.
evidence: This describes the proposed approach in the study.

claim: De novo and data-driven quantitative models were able to cover only a few signaling interactions and therefore had limited predictive power.
source: De novo and data-driven quantitative models were able to cover only a few signaling interactions and therefore had limited predictive power (Nelander et al., 2008; Bender et al., 2011; Klinger et al., 2013; Oates et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous modeling studies.

claim: Qualitative or discrete models can cover more interactions but typically lack the capability of generating quantitative predictions.
source: Qualitative or discrete models can cover more interactions but typically lack the capability of generating quantitative predictions (Saez-Rodriguez et al., 2009; Breitkreutz et al., 2010; Saez-Rodriguez et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous modeling approaches.

claim: Detailed physicochemical models derived using generic biochemical kinetics data can be quite comprehensive and quantitative but typically lack sufficient cell-type specificity required for translationally useful predictions.
source: Detailed physicochemical models derived using generic biochemical kinetics data can be quite comprehensive and quantitative but typically lack sufficient cell-type specificity required for translationally useful predictions (Chen et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous modeling work.

claim: The models constructed in this study capture diverse signaling events and predict cellular response to previously untested combinatorial interventions.
source: The models capture diverse signaling events and predict cellular response to previously untested combinatorial interventions.
evidence: This describes the capabilities of the models developed in the study.

claim: The Pathway Extraction and Reduction Algorithm (PERA) was developed to automatically extract priors from the Pathway Commons signaling information resource.
source: For this purpose, we developed a computational tool (Pathway Extraction and Reduction Algorithm [PERA]) that automatically extracts priors from the Pathway Commons signaling information resource (Demir et al., 2010; Cerami et al., 2011).
evidence: This describes a new computational tool developed in the study.

claim: A BP-based network inference algorithm was previously developed that replaces exhaustive one-by-one searches over many individual network models by a search over probability distributions.
source: To circumvent this problem, we previously had developed a network modeling algorithm based on belief propagation (BP), which replaces exhaustive one-by-one searches over many individual network models by a search over probability distributions representing sets of low-error network models (Molinelli, Korkut, Wang et al., 2013).
evidence: This describes a previously developed algorithm that is used in the current study.

claim: The BP algorithm enables construction of models that can predict response of hundreds of signaling entities to any perturbations in the space of modeled components.
source: The algorithm enables us to construct models that can predict response of hundreds of signaling entities to any perturbations in the space of modeled components.
evidence: This describes the capability of the BP algorithm.

claim: The perturbation biology method was improved through automated incorporation of prior information from signaling databases to obtain more accurate network models.
source: Here, we improved the perturbation biology method through automated incorporation of prior information (signaling interactions from databases) to obtain more accurate network models.
evidence: This describes a key improvement made in the current study.

claim: Prior information is used as soft restraints on search space through use of a probabilistic error model of priors.
source: To improve predictive power and preserve cell-type specificity, we use prior information as soft restraints on search space through use of a probabilistic error model of priors, that is, the algorithm rejects interactions that do not conform to the experimental training data and predicts novel interactions not sampled in the priors (see Equations 2–7).
evidence: This describes the methodological approach for incorporating prior information.

claim: The implementation was scaled up to deal with a larger number of proteomic and phenotypic nodes.
source: To derive richer and more informative network models, we also scaled up the implementation to deal with a larger number of proteomic and phenotypic nodes
evidence: This describes a technical improvement in the implementation.

claim: Network models are simulated with in silico perturbations until the system reaches steady state to quantitatively predict cellular response to combinatorial perturbations.
source: To quantitatively predict cellular response to combinatorial perturbations, we simulate the fully parameterized network models with in silico perturbations until the system reaches steady state (Figure 1).
evidence: This describes the simulation approach used for predictions.

claim: Cell-type specific network models of signaling were constructed from perturbation experiments in RAFi-resistant melanoma cells (SkMel-133 cell line).
source: We constructed cell-type specific network models of signaling from perturbation experiments in RAFi-resistant melanoma cells (SkMel-133 cell line).
evidence: This describes the experimental system used in the study.

claim: The melanoma cells used for network modeling have a BRAFV600E mutation and homozygous deletions in PTEN and CDKN2A.
source: The melanoma cells used for network modeling have a BRAFV600E mutation and homozygous deletions in PTEN and CDKN2A.
evidence: This describes the genetic characteristics of the cell line used.

claim: The models quantitatively link 82 (phospho)proteomic nodes and 12 protein activity nodes with 5 cellular phenotype nodes.
source: The models quantitatively link 82 (phospho)proteomic nodes (i.e., molecular concentrations) and 12 protein activity nodes with 5 cellular phenotype nodes (e.g., cell viability).
evidence: This describes the scope of the network models.

claim: Use of prior information significantly improved the predictive power of the models as shown by cross-validation calculations.
source: As shown by cross-validation calculations, use of prior information significantly improved the predictive power of the models.
evidence: This is a key finding from the validation analysis.

claim: The extent of drug response information was expanded from a few thousand experimental data points to millions of predicted node values.
source: Once the predictive power was established, we expanded the extent of the drug response information from a few thousand experimental data points to millions of predicted node values.
evidence: This describes the scale of predictions generated by the models.

claim: Co-targeting of c-Myc and BRAF or MEK was nominated as a potential strategy to overcome RAFi-resistance based on model predictions.
source: Based on the predictions, which cannot be trivially deduced from experimental data, we nominated co-targeting of c-Myc and BRAF or MEK as a potential strategy to overcome RAFi-resistance.
evidence: This is a key prediction from the computational models.

claim: JQ1 reduces c-Myc expression.
source: To test the prediction, we first experimentally showed that the BET bromodomain inhibitor, JQ1, reduces c-Myc expression.
evidence: This is an experimental observation.

claim: JQ1 blocks the growth of RAFi-resistant SkMel-133 cells in synergy with RAF/MEK signaling inhibition.
source: Next, we showed that JQ1 blocks the growth of RAFi-resistant SkMel-133 cells in synergy with RAF/MEK signaling inhibition, and in this context, overcomes the drug resistance.
evidence: This is an experimental finding validating the model predictions.

claim: JQ1 in combination with RAF/MEK inhibition overcomes drug resistance in SkMel-133 cells.
source: Next, we showed that JQ1 blocks the growth of RAFi-resistant SkMel-133 cells in synergy with RAF/MEK signaling inhibition, and in this context, overcomes the drug resistance.
evidence: This is an experimental finding.

claim: The RAFi-resistant melanoma cell line SkMel-133 was treated with combinations of 12 targeted drugs.
source: The RAFi-resistant melanoma cell line SkMel-133 was treated with combinations of 12 targeted drugs (Figure 2A, see Supplementary file 1A for drug targets and doses, Supplementary file 1C for all perturbation conditions).
evidence: This describes the experimental design.

claim: The perturbations consisted of systematic paired combinations and multiple doses of single agents, generating 89 unique perturbation conditions.
source: The perturbations consisted of systematic paired combinations and multiple doses of single agents. This procedure generated 89 unique perturbation conditions, which targeted specific pathways including those important for melanoma tumorigenesis such as ERK and PI3K/AKT (Haluska et al., 2006).
evidence: This describes the experimental design and scale.

claim: The perturbations targeted specific pathways including those important for melanoma tumorigenesis such as ERK and PI3K/AKT.
source: This procedure generated 89 unique perturbation conditions, which targeted specific pathways including those important for melanoma tumorigenesis such as ERK and PI3K/AKT (Haluska et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citation and describes the experimental design.

claim: Reverse phase protein arrays (RPPA) were used to collect drug response data for 138 proteomic entities in all conditions.
source: We used reverse phase protein arrays (RPPA) to collect drug response data for 138 proteomic (total- and phospho-protein levels) entities in all conditions (Tibes et al., 2006).
evidence: This describes the experimental method used for proteomic profiling.

claim: Phenotypic responses including cell viability and cell cycle progression were measured in all conditions.
source: In parallel, we measured phenotypic responses, including cell viability and cell cycle progression (i.e., G1, S, G2, G2M arrest phenotypes) in all conditions (Figure 2B).
evidence: This describes the phenotypic measurements performed.

claim: Each targeted drug induces a distinct proteomic response in SkMel-133 cells.
source: We demonstrate through hierarchical clustering of the map that each targeted drug induces a distinct proteomic response, and drugs targeting the same pathway lead to overlapping responses in the SkMel-133 cells (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is demonstrated through clustering analysis shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Drugs targeting the same pathway lead to overlapping responses in the SkMel-133 cells.
source: We demonstrate through hierarchical clustering of the map that each targeted drug induces a distinct proteomic response, and drugs targeting the same pathway lead to overlapping responses in the SkMel-133 cells (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is demonstrated through clustering analysis shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Functionally related proteins respond similarly to targeted agents.
source: Through a clustering-driven pathway analysis, we further show that functionally related proteins (i.e., proteins on same or related pathways) respond similarly to targeted agents (Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplements 1–3).
evidence: This is shown through pathway analysis of clustered data.

claim: 82 of the 138 proteomic measurements were included in the network modeling after signal-to-noise analysis.
source: We eliminated such entities from the network modeling with a signal-to-noise analysis and included 82 of the 138 proteomic measurements in the modeling (see 'Materials and methods', Supplementary file 1B).
evidence: This describes the data filtering process for modeling.

claim: Network models contained 99 nodes in total, including 82 proteomic nodes, 5 phenotypic nodes, and 12 activity nodes.
source: In addition to the proteomic nodes, the models contained 5 phenotypic nodes and 12 'activity nodes', which represent the 12 drugs and couple the effects of the targeted perturbations to the other nodes in the network. In total, network models contained 99 nodes.
evidence: This describes the structure of the network models.

claim: The prior information network contains 154 interactions spanning multiple pathways.
source: The prior information network contains 154 interactions spanning multiple pathways (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the prior information extracted from databases.

claim: 4000 distinct and executable model solutions with low errors were generated using the BP-based strategy.
source: Finally, we integrated the experimental data and prior information to generate 4000 distinct and executable model solutions with low errors (i.e., sets of model parameters, Wij, for which the model equations best reproduce the experimental response map) using the BP-based strategy.
evidence: This describes the output of the modeling approach.

claim: A leave-k-out cross validation was performed to assess the predictive power of the network models.
source: To assess the predictive power of the network models (i.e., predicting the response to untested perturbations), we performed a leave-k-out cross validation (Figure 3A).
evidence: This describes the validation methodology.

claim: Network inference with prior information leads to a higher cumulative correlation coefficient and significantly improved prediction quality compared to inference without prior information.
source: In all conditions, network inference with prior information leads to a higher cumulative correlation coefficient (R) and significantly improved prediction quality (RAFi p = 1 × 10−3, AKTi p = 5.7 × 10−3, unpaired t-test H0: ΔXwith_prior = ΔXw/o_prior, ΔX = |Xexp − Xpred|) between experimental and predicted responses.
evidence: This is a key finding from the cross-validation analysis with statistical support.

claim: Use of prior information increased the cumulative correlation coefficient between predicted and experimental response data from 0.72 to 0.84 for RAFi.
source: Use of prior information increased the cumulative correlation coefficient between predicted and experimental response data from 0.72 to 0.84 and from 0.71 to 0.81 for RAFi and AKTi, respectively.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the cross-validation analysis.

claim: Use of prior information increased the cumulative correlation coefficient between predicted and experimental response data from 0.71 to 0.81 for AKTi.
source: Use of prior information increased the cumulative correlation coefficient between predicted and experimental response data from 0.72 to 0.84 and from 0.71 to 0.81 for RAFi and AKTi, respectively.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the cross-validation analysis.

claim: The average network model contains 202 unique interactions (127 activating and 75 inhibitory interactions) between 99 signaling entities.
source: The average model contains 202 unique interactions (127 activating and 75 inhibitory interactions) between 99 signaling entities.
evidence: This describes the structure of the average network model.

claim: 89 of the 154 interactions in the prior model conform to the experimental data and are included in the average model.
source: 89 of the 154 interactions in the prior model conform to the experimental data, and therefore, are accepted in the majority of the model solutions by the inference algorithm and included in the average model (Figure 4—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This describes how prior information was validated against experimental data.

claim: Models recapitulate many known interactions in pathways important in melanoma tumorigenesis.
source: The subnetwork diagrams indicate that models recapitulate many known interactions in pathways, which are important in melanoma tumorigenesis (e.g., PI3K/AKT and ERK) and nominate previously unidentified interactions (see Figure 4 legend).
evidence: This is shown through analysis of the network subnetworks.

claim: The simulations expand the size of the response map by three orders of magnitude.
source: The simulations expand the size of the response map by three orders of magnitude (i.e., from few thousand experimental response data to millions of predicted responses) (Figure 5C, Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the scale of predictions generated.

claim: In silico perturbations of c-Myc lead to the strongest G1-arrest response when c-Myc is co-targeted with BRAF, MEK, and cyclin D1.
source: In particular, in silico perturbations of c-Myc lead to the strongest G1-arrest response when c-Myc is co-targeted with BRAF, MEK, and cyclin D1 (Figures 5D–H, 6A).
evidence: This is a key prediction from the model simulations.

claim: Induction of G1-arrest is a promising strategy for controlling melanoma growth.
source: The G1-arrest phenotype is of particular interest given that induction of G1-arrest is a promising strategy for controlling melanoma growth (Solit et al., 2006)
evidence: This is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: Various genomic alterations associated with G1/S transition are involved in tumor progression.
source: The G1-arrest phenotype is of particular interest given that induction of G1-arrest is a promising strategy for controlling melanoma growth (Solit et al., 2006) and various genomic alterations associated with G1/S transition are involved in tumor progression (Rother and Jones, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: c-Myc links multiple pathways such as ERK and PI3K/AKT to regulation of cell cycle arrest.
source: Consistent with the vast literature on c-Myc's role in genesis of many cancers (Dang, 2012), predictions indicated that c-Myc linked multiple pathways such as ERK and PI3K/AKT to regulation of cell cycle arrest (Table 1; also see Figure 6—figure supplement 2 for the highly complex c-Myc response to targeted perturbations in the underlying RPPA data).
evidence: This is inferred from the model predictions and supported by literature citation.

claim: JQ1 is a BRD4 inhibitor that negatively affects c-Myc transcription.
source: To test our predictions, we targeted c-Myc using the epigenetic drug JQ1, a BRD4 inhibitor that negatively affects c-Myc transcription (Delmore et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: Combinations of JQ1 with MEKi or RAFi synergistically induced G1-arrest in SkMel-133 cells.
source: We treated SkMel-133 cells with combinations of JQ1 and MEKi or RAFi and showed that both combinations synergistically induced G1-arrest and decreased cell viability.
evidence: This is an experimental finding.

claim: Combinations of JQ1 with MEKi or RAFi decreased cell viability in SkMel-133 cells.
source: We treated SkMel-133 cells with combinations of JQ1 and MEKi or RAFi and showed that both combinations synergistically induced G1-arrest and decreased cell viability.
evidence: This is an experimental finding.

claim: The cell viability IC50s for RAFi and MEKi in SkMel-133 cells are at least one order of magnitude higher than the doses required to reduce phosphorylation of immediate downstream targets by 50%.
source: In SkMel-133 cells, however, the cell viability IC50s for RAFi and MEKi are at least one order of magnitude higher than the doses required to reduce the phosphorylation of immediate downstream targets (phospho-MEK and phospho-ERK) by 50% (Figure 6B, Table 2), and hence, the cells are considered to be relatively resistant to both drugs.
evidence: This is an experimental observation demonstrating drug resistance.

claim: When combined with JQ1, the concentrations of RAFi/MEKi that are sufficient to reduce cell viability by 50% are in the range of MEK and ERK phosphorylation IC50s.
source: When combined with JQ1, the concentrations of RAFi/MEKi that are sufficient to reduce cell viability by 50% are in the range of MEK and ERK phosphorylation IC50s (Table 2).
evidence: This is an experimental finding showing the effect of the drug combination.

claim: The combination of JQ1 affecting c-Myc levels and a FLT3 tyrosine kinase inhibitor was synergistic in overcoming resistance to the FLT3 TKI in acute myeloid leukemia cells in an independent study.
source: Interestingly, in an independent study in hematopoietic cancer, the combination of JQ1 affecting the c-Myc levels and a FLT3 tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) was synergistic in overcoming resistance to the FLT3 TKI in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) cells (Fiskus et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to an independent study.

claim: This study is the first demonstration of a combined inhibition of a BET bromodomain protein and a protein kinase molecule to overcome drug resistance in solid tumors.
source: As far as we know, our study is the first demonstration of a combined inhibition of a BET bromodomain (BET-BRD) protein and a protein kinase molecule to overcome drug resistance in solid tumors (Filippakopoulos and Knapp, 2014).
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the findings.

claim: c-Myc is a multifunctional transcription factor with a central role in cell cycle progression and receives inputs from diverse signaling pathways.
source: To interpret these positive results, we note that c-Myc is a multifunctional transcription factor with a central role in cell cycle progression and receives inputs from diverse signaling pathways, including ERK, PI3K/AKT, Wnt, and TGF-β signaling (Dang, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: c-Myc may be a particular 'point of vulnerability' in RAFi drug-resistant cells.
source: We hypothesize that, beyond the efficacy of co-targeting BRAF kinase and c-Myc, there may be a particular advantage in blocking proliferative signals from various oncogenic pathways that converge on the downstream effector c-Myc. In other words, c-Myc may be a particular 'point of vulnerability' in RAFi drug-resistant cells (Figure 7)
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the experimental findings.

claim: Synergistic co-targeting of a key genomic aberration and a downstream point of convergence of signaling may be a more effective way of overcoming resistance than co-targeting another upstream pathway.
source: We suggest that synergistic co-targeting of a key genomic aberration (e.g., BRAFV600E) and a downstream point of convergence of signaling (e.g., c-Myc) may be a more effective way of overcoming the resistance than co-targeting another upstream pathway (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed based on the study findings.

claim: The upstream–downstream combination of targets may have the dual advantage of generality in overcoming resistance and avoidance of toxicity.
source: In other words, the upstream–downstream combination of targets may have the dual advantage of generality in overcoming resistance and avoidance of toxicity.
evidence: This is a hypothesis about the potential advantages of the proposed strategy.

claim: JQ1 has been reported to have poor in vivo efficacy with low metabolic stability and bio-solubility.
source: Unfortunately, the widely used investigational BET-BRD inhibitor JQ1 has been reported to have poor in vivo efficacy with low metabolic stability and bio-solubility, but fortunately, other BET-BRD inhibitors with more promising pharmacokinetic properties have been and are being developed.
evidence: This is based on reported properties of JQ1 in the literature.

claim: JQ1 reaches a maximum blood concentration of 0.84 μM in mouse models.
source: Specifically, JQ1 is reported to have a maximum blood concentration of 0.84 μM in mouse models, whereas the compounds I-BET-762 and I-BET-151 reach maximum blood concentrations of 26 μM and 82 μM, respectively (Dawson et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published pharmacokinetic data.

claim: I-BET-762 reaches a maximum blood concentration of 26 μM in mouse models.
source: Specifically, JQ1 is reported to have a maximum blood concentration of 0.84 μM in mouse models, whereas the compounds I-BET-762 and I-BET-151 reach maximum blood concentrations of 26 μM and 82 μM, respectively (Dawson et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published pharmacokinetic data.

claim: I-BET-151 reaches a maximum blood concentration of 82 μM in mouse models.
source: Specifically, JQ1 is reported to have a maximum blood concentration of 0.84 μM in mouse models, whereas the compounds I-BET-762 and I-BET-151 reach maximum blood concentrations of 26 μM and 82 μM, respectively (Dawson et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published pharmacokinetic data.

claim: Triazolobenzodiazepine and triazolothienodiazepine BET-BRD inhibitors are reported to be stable in liver microsomes and have up to 30% bioavailability.
source: In general, triazolobenzodiazepine (e.g., I-BET-762 and I-BET-151 compounds) and triazolothienodiazepine (e.g., OTX015, TEN-010, CPI-0610 compounds) BET-BRD inhibitors are reported to be stable in liver microsomes and have up to 30% bioavailability.
evidence: This is based on reported properties of these compounds.

claim: Several clinical trials of BET-BRD inhibitors have been initiated in multiple cancer types.
source: Several clinical trials of BET-BRD inhibitors with desirable pharmacokinetic properties have been initiated in multiple cancer types, including trials with OTX015 for the treatment of acute leukemia (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT01713582), CPI-0610 for progressive lymphoma (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT01949883), I-BET-762 and TEN-010 for NUT midline carcinoma (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT01587703, NCT01987362), and a dose escalation and cohort expansion study for TEN-010 in patients with AML and myelodysplastic syndrome (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT02308761).
evidence: This is factual information about ongoing clinical trials.

claim: The model-based predictions provide comprehensive and testable hypotheses on complex signaling mechanisms relevant to the development of novel therapies.
source: The model-based predictions provide comprehensive and testable hypotheses on complex signaling mechanisms relevant to the development of novel therapies.
evidence: This is a summary statement about the utility of the approach.

claim: More comprehensive experimental data and improvements in signaling databases are likely to lead to network models with even higher predictive power.
source: More comprehensive experimental data and improvements in signaling databases are likely to lead to network models with even higher predictive power.
evidence: This is a speculation about future improvements.

claim: The perturbation biology method paves the way for model-driven quantitative cell biology with diverse applications in many fields of biology.
source: Based on these results, we put forward the falsifiable hypothesis that co-targeting a specific upstream alteration and a general downstream point of vulnerability is a good strategy to prevent or overcome resistance to targeted drugs.
evidence: This is a broad claim about the potential impact of the method.

claim: Oncogenic alterations that affect sensitivity to targeted therapies may pre-exist in the tumor before treatment or emerge sequentially as the result of treatment.
source: Oncogenic alterations that affect sensitivity to targeted therapies may pre-exist in the tumor before treatment or emerge sequentially as the result of treatment.
evidence: This is established knowledge about tumor evolution and drug resistance.

claim: Tumors can escape drug treatment through diverse routes and dominant mechanisms of resistance are the exception.
source: Tumors can escape drug treatment through diverse routes and dominant mechanisms of resistance are the exception (such as the T790M mutation in EGFR, which confers resistance to EGFR inhibitors in many patients as well as in the laboratory [Pao et al., 2005])
evidence: This is supported by citation and represents established knowledge.

claim: PTEN loss was associated with resistance to RAFi in BRAFV600E mutated melanoma.
source: For example, PTEN loss was associated with resistance to RAFi (in BRAFV600E mutated melanoma) and as a result joint inhibition of BRAF and PI3K was proposed as a combination therapy (Villanueva et al., 2010; Xing et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published research.

claim: Joint inhibition of BRAF and PI3K was proposed as a combination therapy for PTEN loss-associated resistance.
source: For example, PTEN loss was associated with resistance to RAFi (in BRAFV600E mutated melanoma) and as a result joint inhibition of BRAF and PI3K was proposed as a combination therapy (Villanueva et al., 2010; Xing et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published research.

claim: Tumor cells rapidly adapt and escape through alternate routes after a brief period of response to combination therapy in almost all cases.
source: For almost all cases, however, tumor cells rapidly adapt and escape through alternate routes after a brief period of response to the combination.
evidence: This is a general observation about the limitations of combination therapies.
